subject: ACMEBank — region pinning & cross-region failover questions
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: John Smith <john.smith@acmebank.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: ACMEbank region pinning & failover — next steps

Thanks again for taking the time this morning, John — good conversation. Quick recap and a couple of clarifying Qs so we can put together a formal design + SOW: 

Summary
- Primary goal: ensure customer data for EU customers remains in-region (EU) by default; US region will serve US customers.
- Need an operational plan for cross-region failover (DR) and backups, and specifics on logging/audit access for your security team.

Action items / clarifying questions from Redwood
1) Region scope: please confirm which geo(s) need strict in-region residency (US, EU, APAC). Is it per-customer/account or per-tenant?
2) Cross-region failover: are you comfortable with active-passive failover within the same region group (e.g., EU-primary -> EU-secondary) vs. cross-continent failover (EU -> US) for DR? If cross-continent failover is allowed, are there legal constraints we should be aware of (e.g., data export restrictions)?
3) Backups: retention window required for PII/backups and any encryption/KMS requirements (customer-managed KMS?).
4) Logs & audit: retention window for request logs, whether full request/response logs (redacted) can be stored, and whether you require push of logs to your SIEM (S3/syslog) or will pull via API.

Attachments: redwood-region-pinning-diagram.png (network/replication diagram).

Next steps
- If you can reply with the questions above, we'll produce a concise design doc with region pinning options and a proposed failover policy.
- I’ll loop in our Solutions Architect (Marissa) after we get your answers so she can map to an implementation and cost estimate.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com | (415) 555-0132

From: John Smith <john.smith@acmebank.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: security@acmebank.com
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: ACMEbank region pinning & failover — next steps

Aditya — thanks for the recap. Answers inline below.

1) Region scope: Primary requirement is that EU customer data remains in EU. We also have APAC customers (mostly APAC India region) but that's lower priority for phase 1. Residency requirement: per-customer/account.

2) Cross-region failover: We can accept cross-region failover for disaster scenarios but only with full encryption-in-flight and at-rest, and only if data access is auditable. Prefer failover to another EU region for EU customers; cross-continent (EU->US) as absolute last resort and requires legal sign-off.

3) Backups: PII backups retained for 90 days. We require customer-managed KMS for keys used to encrypt backups of sensitive content (we prefer BYOK via AWS KMS / GCP KMS).

4) Logs & audit: We need request-level metadata and audit logs retained for 1 year. Full request/response logging for research is allowed if sensitive fields are redacted. Ideally logs should be pushed to our S3 bucket (encrypted) and also available via API for on-demand review.

Attached is a short spreadsheet with answers and the compliance contacts who will be involved: security@acmebank.com.

Thanks — happy to sync again once you have the proposed design.

John Smith
Senior Product Manager, Platform
ACME Bank
john.smith@acmebank.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: John Smith <john.smith@acmebank.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 13:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: ACMEbank region pinning & failover — next steps

John — thanks for the quick answers, very helpful. A few clarifications from the implementation side and a proposed approach below.

Proposed approach (high level)- Region pinning: we'll support per-account region tagging. Requests include a region attribute and our routing will prefer the pinned region. For EU-pinned accounts, data (model inputs, outputs, and derived artifacts) and backups will be stored in EU regions by default.
- Failover model: two options:
  * Active-passive within region family (recommended): EU-primary -> EU-secondary (same jurisdiction). Automatic failover with health checks; sessions/KV cache rehydration strategy documented.
  * Cross-continent (EU->US) failover: supported only as an opt-in DR mode and requires additional contract language + compliance sign-off. We will log every cross-region access and provide audit artifacts.
- Backups: encrypted at-rest with customer-managed KMS optional. Snapshots are stored in-region by default; we can enable cross-region replication only if you sign off and accept the data egress conditions. Retention policy is configurable — default PII backup retention template is 90 days (we can extend).
- Logs & delivery: we can push structured audit logs to your encrypted S3 bucket (preferred) or deliver to your SIEM via syslog connector. Request/response payloads marked as sensitive will be automatically redacted; we also provide controls to configure redaction rules. Retention for audit logs can be set to 1 year; we can provide a dedicated retention policy per account.

Questions we still have
- For customer-managed KMS, do you want Redwood to support automatic key rotation or will you manage rotation on your side?
- For the cross-region DR option, please confirm the legal owner who will sign the DR addendum.

Attached: acme-data-residency-answers.xlsx (answers + compliance contacts). Design doc draft: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-region-pinning-design
HubSpot: https://hubspot.com/deal/ACME-12345
